summary.headline: S.P. Apparels Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell to INR 364 crore (from INR 399 crore) and EBITDA margin to 12.2%; management guides INR 2,000 crore FY27 revenue.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was soft on volumes: consolidated revenue declined year-on-year to INR 364 crore and EBITDA to INR 44 crore, with PAT down to INR 18.59 crore, as US tariff after-effects and shipping disruption delayed orders. Full-year consolidated revenue grew 13.2% to INR 1,578 crore and EBITDA rose 16% to INR 217 crore. Management says US orders are returning, guides to INR 2,000 crore consolidated revenue in FY27, and points to Sri Lanka ramp-up and EU/UK FTA benefits. Current utilisation is cited at 64%, and the timing of recovery in H2 FY27 is the key uncertainty.

segments.name: Garment division incl. Young Brand (FY26)
segments.commentary: Operational revenue INR 1,421.98 crore (vs INR 1,308.18 crore) and EBITDA INR 230.57 crore (vs INR 212.18 crore). Q4 garment revenue was INR 316 crore, flat against the prior-year quarter, and Q4 EBITDA fell to INR 51.41 crore from INR 58.20 crore.

segments.name: Young Brand Apparel
segments.commentary: FY26 adjusted revenue INR 321.26 crore and adjusted EBITDA INR 49.23 crore; Q4 adjusted revenue INR 66.88 crore (vs INR 81.37 crore) and adjusted EBITDA INR 8.47 crore (vs INR 12.85 crore). Business is 100% US-customer based and was hit by tariffs.

segments.name: SPUK (UK)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue GBP 7.5 million (INR 87.04 crore) with positive EBITDA of INR 1.10 crore. Q4 revenue was INR 35.04 crore vs INR 18.34 crore a year earlier. Order book is GBP 6.1 million.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 71.54 crore (vs INR 79.41 crore); EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 6.1 crore from INR 6.84 crore. Management says Retail was EBITDA-positive from Q2 to Q4 FY26, and that finance cost, not depreciation, keeps it PAT-negative.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue target of INR 2,000 crore at 14-15% EBITDA margin (management said the 15% applies to the Garmenting division, not consolidated).
FY27 revenue split given as INR 1,800 crore Garmenting (incl. Young Brand and Sri Lanka), INR 150 crore SPUK, INR 80-90 crore Retail.
Core government export business targeted at 17-18% adjusted EBITDA margin as operating leverage improves.
Sri Lanka FOB target of INR 200-250 crore in FY27 and INR 400-450 crore in FY28; the acquired capacity is capable of about INR 400 crore.
Peak capacity revenue around INR 2,500 crore (FY28 indicated), requiring about 9,000-10,000 machines.
SPUK FY27 revenue expected at GBP 12-14 million; SPUK EBITDA margin guided at 4-5%.
Targeted geographic mix of US 30%, Europe 35%, UK 35% by FY27 (US currently 17% in Q4, 22% previously).
Solar capacity target of about 4.5 MW by March 2027.
Possible contingent upside from customer reimbursement of tariff-related discount credits; not booked until received.
capex_capacity: India machines planned at 5,700 in FY27 versus the earlier 6,000 target; Sivakasi 440-machine expansion slowed due to US tariff uncertainty. Management said recruitment has restarted, with Sivakasi expected at 200-300 machines in about three months.
Sri Lanka: first factory operations began around mid-April 2026; scaling to four factories within 12 months; about 2,000 machines planned in FY27.

Salem (Young Brand) expansion of about 300 machines, worth INR 50-60 crore revenue, now expected to contribute in FY28 after about six months to commercial production; 1,400 Young Brand machines in FY27.
Adding 300 machines costs about INR 200-250 crore; management said capacity is not the constraint, people are.
Current utilisation is 64% in the quarter; management cites 90% as optimum. No further capacity expansion planned for FY28 until utilisation rises.
demand_pricing: Order book: SPAL Garmenting INR 380 crore, Young Brand INR 142 crore, SPUK GBP 6.1 million; total about INR 600 crore.
US customers returning with orders; management expects the pace to improve from August 2026. Lead time from order to shipment is 90-120 days.
Realisations stated as broadly intact; Q4 softness was volume-led rather than price-led. Raw material and yarn prices up about 5%; some pass-through to customers accepted.
Cotton price rose to about INR 75,000 per candle and has eased to about INR 70,000.

Rupee depreciation (about 95-96 per USD vs 90 earlier) is cited as helping competitiveness against Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, though CFO said 80% of orders are hedged on booking, so no direct pricing benefit is captured.

Management says customers are shifting orders from Bangladesh to India ahead of Bangladesh losing EU duty-free status by 2029; UK and EU FTAs expected within 2-3 months, with benefits mainly volume rather than price.
Group has 12 customers: about 4-5 US (incl. Young Brand) and 7-8 Europe/UK.

qa_highlights.question: Is rupee depreciation driving incremental volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said duty-paid status versus duty-free Bangladesh and Sri Lanka helps competitiveness and is bringing more business. The CFO added that 80% of orders are covered when booked, so there is no direct benefit from depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 2,000 crore FY27 target be reached, given Sri Lanka and Sivakasi ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sri Lanka FOB is about INR 45 crore in FY26, targeting INR 200-250 crore in FY27. Sivakasi adds about INR 40-50 crore, and H2 FY27 is expected to see the recovery as utilisation rises from 64%. Analyst arithmetic came to about INR 1,850 crore, and the gap was not fully bridged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% margin guidance on consolidated or Garmenting basis?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the 14-15% margin applies to consolidated figures in one answer, and later said the 15% applies to the Garmenting division only, with INR 2,000 crore on a consolidated basis. The basis is therefore ambiguous.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SPUK revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: SPUK has an order book of GBP 6 million and is targeting a further GBP 6-8 million for FY27, for GBP 12-14 million in total. Two anchor customers are each expected to give about GBP 8 million, and 2-3 more customers are being added.

qa_highlights.question: Will Retail become PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said Retail is at EBITDA breakeven, and that finance cost on Retail Ventures is the drag. He said equity raising is needed and the company is ready to raise it now.

qa_highlights.question: Has labour returned after the capacity cut?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said workers left after the US capacity reduction, and that 30-40% have returned. Recruitment and training are ongoing, and management said this is not a labour disruption.

risks_watch: Timing of US order recovery: management expects pace to improve from August 2026, and Q1-Q2 FY27 are described as still affected by tariff after-effects.
Execution of the INR 2,000 crore FY27 target: it relies on H2 utilisation recovery, from 64% currently, and on Sri Lanka scaling to INR 200-250 crore.
Margin basis ambiguity: 14-15% consolidated versus 15% Garmenting-only, plus raw material cost pass-through.
Contingent tariff discount-credit reimbursement, timing outside management control.
Retail equity raise and finance cost; SPUK margin still low at 4-5%.
FTA timing: UK and EU FTAs were expected within 2-3 months but have been delayed before.
Labour re-hiring and training; only 30-40% of workers expected to return.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the medium-term story (INR 2,000 crore FY27 target, Sri Lanka scale-up, FTA and Bangladesh duty-free tailwinds) but cautious and evasive on near-term specifics. Answers on the H2 FY27 bridge, the 14-15% margin basis, the Sivakasi and Salem timing, and the Retail equity raise were inconsistent or deferred, and the CFO corrected the margin basis mid-call.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 consolidated revenue of INR 2,000 crore (about 27% above FY26's INR 1,578 crore) at 14-15% EBITDA, backed by an INR 600 crore order book, Sri Lanka ramp-up (INR 200-250 crore FOB target) and SPUK GBP 12-14 million, but Indian expansion is deferred, utilisation is only 64%, and the H2 FY27 recovery timing is uncertain.
